newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares slide amid profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares slide amid profit-taking.

text.p: Turkish shares slimmed earlier gains on Monday amid profit-taking sales in volatile trade, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 lost 0.49 percent or 315.67 points to end at 64,666.57, off from an earlier session high of 65,596.23.
Daily volume dropped to 7.8 trillion lira from Friday's 8.4 trillion lira.
"There were profit-taking sales after selective activity. I think this shows horizontal trade will continue unless there is fresh cash inflow," said Turgay Uzuner from Global Securities.
Brokers said they expected trade to be squeezed between 63,000 and 65,000 in the next days until there were fresh market-moving news to stir activity.
The session's most active shares were those of Isbank, losing 500 lira to 9,000 lira. Shares of utility Aktas followed, staying steady at 480,000 lira.
Isbank shares slimmed gains in profit-taking after surging on news that the bank's half-year profits rose to 9.1 trillion lira in first half 1995, up from 5.06 trillion in the same period last year.
The 85-share industrial index lost 0.02 percent to 71,249.40 and the 15-share financial index dived by 1.67 percent to 56,640.84.
Of the 219 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 85 to 81 and 53 were steady.
